$comment: Neutral shipped <memory.h> — c81 (the sqlite shell.c CLI route; shell.c:7121 [base85.c] `#include <memory.h>` — UNCONDITIONAL, not !_WIN32-guarded). <memory.h> is the pre-ANSI legacy alias of <string.h> (historically it provided the mem* family; every modern libc ships it as a string.h forwarder — glibc /usr/include/memory.h is literally `#include <string.h>`, MSVC CRT and Darwin ship the same alias). The simplest CORRECT neutral form is a descriptor that MIRRORS string.json's mem* surface byte-for-byte (the descriptor model has no `aliasOf`; an empty descriptor fails loud by design — 'declares nothing'). DOUBLE-INCLUDE IS SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: shell.c includes BOTH <string.h> (166 etc.) and <memory.h> — the semantic injection dedups symbol names FIRST-WINS across descriptors (semantic_analyzer FF11 `injectedNames`), so exactly ONE memcpy extern is minted per CU regardless of which header (or both) appears; a TU including ONLY <memory.h> still resolves the mem* family. str* names are deliberately NOT mirrored: historical memory.h provided only the mem* family, and shipping less keeps the alias honest (a str* user includes <string.h>). UNGATED (no availableObjectFormats) + the full tri-format library map, exactly like string.json — the header exists on every platform and shell.c's include is unconditional, so a windows-pe shell.c build must resolve it too. | pe UCRT migration Phase 1 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): pe `library` msvcrt.dll -> ucrtbase.dll. The mem* family is STATELESS — memcpy/memmove/memset/memcmp/memchr read and write only CALLER-OWNED buffers and touch no CRT global state (no heap, no FILE*, no errno, no locale) — so sourcing them from ucrtbase while the rest of a program still binds msvcrt is safe under the migration's CO-STATE-GROUP rule (a heap ptr / FILE* / fd / errno / static tm made by one CRT and read by the other corrupts SILENTLY; a value->value call cannot). ★ NOTE the asymmetry with the string.json rows this descriptor mirrors: string.json STAYS on msvcrt until Phase 3 because `_strdup` RETURNS A CRT-HEAP POINTER the program later free()s — a genuine co-state coupling the mem* family does not have. The first-wins dedup above is unaffected by the split binding: dedup is by symbol NAME and the mem* names are byte-identical in both descriptors, so a TU including both headers still mints exactly one extern (whichever descriptor is injected first supplies its library binding). All 5 symbols verified present in the live ucrtbase.dll export table per D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT.
